hints: Focus on what type of hybridisation each carbon has in ethene, since that tells you which orbitals are available for bonding.
Remember the C-C sigma bond in ethene comes from head-on overlap of two directional $sp^2$ hybrid orbitals along the bond axis.
Compare head-on overlap along the axis with sideways overlap above and below, and pick the diagram that shows direct end-to-end overlap between the two carbons.
walkthrough:
**Recall the bonding in ethene**

Each carbon in $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ forms three sigma bonds and one pi bond. That means each carbon is $sp^2$ hybridised.

$$\text{C in ethene: } 1 \times 2s + 2 \times 2p \rightarrow 3 \times sp^2 + 1 \times p$$

**Identify the C-C sigma bond**

The sigma bond between the two carbons is formed by direct, head-on overlap along the internuclear axis. For ethene this is $sp^2$ overlapping with $sp^2$.

$$\sigma_{C-C} = sp^2 + sp^2 \text{ (head-on)}$$

**Match to the diagram**

Look for two directional, lobe-shaped hybrid orbitals pointing at each other and overlapping end-to-end. That is the central overlap in diagram C, where the outer small lobes then bond to hydrogen. Sideways overlap is the pi bond, not the sigma bond.

options.A: Shows overlap of two simple spherical orbitals. This looks like s-s overlap, such as in $\text{H}_2$, not the directional $sp^2$-$sp^2$ head-on overlap between carbons in ethene.
options.B: Shows orbitals of mismatched size and shape overlapping. It does not show two identical directional $sp^2$ hybrids meeting head-on along the C-C axis, so it cannot be the C-C sigma bond.
options.C: Correct. The middle overlap shows two $sp^2$ hybrid orbitals, one from each carbon, overlapping head-on to form the C-C sigma bond. The outer small orbitals represent the sigma bonds to hydrogen. This is exactly the $sp^2$-$sp^2$ sigma framework of ethene.
options.D: Shows sideways overlap of unhybridised p orbitals above and below the bond axis. That forms the C-C pi bond in ethene, not the sigma bond. A common trap is to confuse pi overlap with sigma overlap.
